core_obligations: Cover X by finitely many affine opens and attach to each a cardinal beyond which the base change of that piece is Jacobson with algebraic residue fields at closed points (proof lines 2713-2719).
Take the maximum of those cardinals and note that for any extension of larger cardinality every affine piece satisfies the conclusions (proof lines 2720-2722).
Apply the local criterion for Jacobson schemes to conclude that X_K is Jacobson, and inherit the residue field statement from the affine pieces (proof lines 2722-2726).
proof_roadmap: Cardinal thresholds for the affine pieces (proof lines 2713-2719).
Global Jacobson property and residue fields (proof lines 2722-2726).
difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over a field k, the lemma asserts that for every field extension K/k of sufficiently large cardinality, the residue field at every closed point of X_K is algebraic over K and X_K is a Jacobson scheme (statement lines 2699-2710). The proof covers X by affine opens, uses the algebra base change result for Jacobson rings and the affine criterion to attach to each member U_i a cardinal kappa_i beyond which the base change U_{i,K} has both properties, takes the maximum of the finitely many cardinals, and then applies the local criterion for Jacobson schemes to conclude for X_K (proof lines 2712-2723). The statement about residue fields is inherited from the affine members (proof lines 2724-2726). The claim is H2: a compact argument whose content is the passage from the affine pieces to the global scheme, with the cardinal threshold bookkeeping written out.
